leads_to.evidence: Business graduates mostly go straight to work without a license. BLS counts general and operations manager as the bachelor's-level job with the most openings. Higher-paying roles like management analyst also expect several years of experience or an MBA.

nearby_pair.evidence: Cal State LA admits first-year students, and Fremont University's Cerritos campus admits anyone with a high school diploma or GED. A new student in the Los Angeles area could choose either one.

school_matters.evidence: Business pay barely changes across schools that admit over a quarter of applicants. Schools that admit under a quarter feed banks and consultancies: at Michigan's Ross business school, 42.9% of 2023 BBAs went into financial services and 24.8% into consulting.

who_is_counted.evidence: The largest programs include online and pooled programs at schools like WGU, where four in five students work while enrolled and the average age is about 36. These graduates are mostly working adults, while traditional campuses enroll new graduates.

programs.evidence: Bismarck State's online applied bachelor's in energy management admits only students who already hold an associate degree, certificate or diploma in electric power technology. Its students are already utility and power plant workers.
Michigan's Ross business school sends most of its BBA graduates to financial services and consulting firms such as PwC Strategy&, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and Boston Consulting Group.

City University of Seattle's business bachelor's is a degree-completion program for working professionals and adult learners. It accepts up to 90 lower-division transfer credits and offers part-time study.
